items.title: Review duplicate generated source-line IDs in mesh API reference
items.body:
The mesh API reference published by #459 has unique API/heading anchors, but multiple expandable source blocks from GeomMeshDataclasses produce duplicate generated line IDs (for example `__span-0-60` and `__codelineno-0-60`). The local final strict build detected 52 duplicated source-line identifiers on this page; strict MkDocs validation does not flag them. The production page also passes the API/heading anchor checks.

Please review mkdocstrings/Pymdown source rendering so each source snippet gets a unique line-ID prefix without removing source visibility or breaking public API anchors. This is a renderer/navigation follow-up, not a hydraulic or API execution defect.

Acceptance criteria:
- No repeated IDs within the generated mesh reference page.
- Expandable source code, syntax highlighting and API signature rendering remain usable.
- Public method and result-class anchor URLs remain stable.
- Verify on the built HTML, not just Markdown or a successful strict build.

Page: https://rascommander.info/ras/api/rasmapper/mesh-generation/

items.title: Admonitions - Material for MkDocs
items.body:
[](https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/edit/master/docs/reference/admonitions.md "Edit this page")[](https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/raw/master/docs/reference/admonitions.md "View source of this page")

Admonitions, also known as _call-outs_, are an excellent choice for including side content without significantly interrupting the document flow. Material for MkDocs provides several different types of admonitions and allows for the inclusion and nesting of arbitrary content.

Configuration[¶](#configuration "Permanent link")
-------------------------------------------------

This configuration enables admonitions, allows to make them collapsible and to nest arbitrary content inside admonitions. Add the following lines to `mkdocs.yml`:

`[](#__codelineno-0-1)markdown_extensions:
 [](#__codelineno-0-2)  -  admonition [](#__codelineno-0-3)  -  pymdownx.details [](#__codelineno-0-4)  -  pymdownx.superfences` 

See additional configuration options:

*   [Admonition](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/extensions/python-markdown/#admonition)
*   [Details](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/extensions/python-markdown-extensions/#details)
*   [SuperFences](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/extensions/python-markdown-extensions/#superfences)

### Admonition icons[¶](#admonition-icons "Permanent link")

[8.3.0](https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/releases/tag/8.3.0)

Each of the supported admonition types has a distinct icon, which can be changed to any icon bundled with the theme, or even a [custom icon](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/changing-the-logo-and-icons/#additional-icons). Add the following lines to `mkdocs.yml`:

`[](#__codelineno-1-1)theme:
 [](#__codelineno-1-2)  icon: [](#__codelineno-1-3)  admonition: [](#__codelineno-1-4)  <type>:  <icon>` 

Expand to show alternate icon sets

`[](#__codelineno-2-1)theme:
 [](#__codelineno-2-2)  icon: [](#__codelineno-2-3)  admonition: [](#__codelineno-2-4)  note:  octicons/tag-16 [](#__codelineno-2-5)  abstract:  octicons/checklist-16 [](#__codelineno-2-6)  info:  octicons/info-16 [](#__codelineno-2-7)  tip:  octicons/squirrel-16 [](#__codelineno-2-8)  success:  octicons/check-16 [](#__codelineno-2-9)  question:  octicons/question-16 [](#__codelineno-2-10)  warning:  octicons/alert-16 [](#__codelineno-2-11)  failure:  octicons/x-circle-16 [](#__codelineno-2-12)  danger:  octicons/zap-16 [](#__codelineno-2-13)  bug:  octicons/bug-16 [](#__codelineno-2-14)  example:  octicons/beaker-16 [](#__codelineno-2-15)  quote:  octicons/quote-16` 

`[](#__codelineno-3-1)theme:
 [](#__codelineno-3-2)  icon: [](#__codelineno-3-3)  admonition: [](#__codelineno-3-4)  note:  fontawesome/solid/note-sticky [](#__codelineno-3-5)  abstract:  fontawesome/solid/book [](#__codelineno-3-6)  info:  fontawesome/solid/circle-info [](#__codelineno-3-7)  tip:  fontawesome/solid/bullhorn [](#__codelineno-3-8)  success:  fontawesome/solid/check [](#__codelineno-3-9)  question:  fontawesome/solid/circle-question [](#__codelineno-3-10)  warning:  fontawesome/solid/triangle-exclamation [](#__codelineno-3-11)  failure:  fontawesome/solid/bomb [](#__codelineno-3-12)  danger:  fontawesome/solid/skull [](#__codelineno-3-13)  bug:  fontawesome/solid/robot [](#__codelineno-3-14)  example:  fontawesome/solid/flask [](#__codelineno-3-15)  quote:  fontawesome/solid/quote-left` 

Usage[¶](#usage "Permanent link")
---------------------------------

Admonitions follow a simple syntax: a block starts with `!!!`, followed by a single keyword used as a [type qualifier](#supported-types). The content of the block follows on the next line, indented by four spaces:

Admonition

`[](#__codelineno-4-1)!!! note   [](#__codelineno-4-3)    Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Nulla et euismod [](#__codelineno-4-4)    nulla. Curabitur feugiat, tortor non consequat finibus, justo purus auctor [](#__codelineno-4-5)    massa, nec semper lorem quam in massa.` 

Note

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Nulla et euismod nulla. Curabitur feugiat, tortor non consequat finibus, justo purus auctor massa, nec semper lorem quam in massa.

### Changing the title[¶](#changing-the-title "Permanent link")

By default, the title will equal the type qualifier in titlecase. However, it can be changed by adding a quoted string containing valid Markdown (including links, formatting, ...) after the type qualifier:

Admonition with custom title

`[](#__codelineno-5-1)!!! note "Phasellus posuere in sem ut cursus"   [](#__codelineno-5-3)    Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Nulla et euismod [](#__codelineno-5-4)    nulla. Curabitur feugiat, tortor non consequat finibus, justo purus auctor [](#__codelineno-5-5)    massa, nec semper lorem quam in massa.` 

Phasellus posuere in sem ut cursus

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Nulla et euismod nulla. Curabitur feugiat, tortor non consequat finibus, justo purus auctor massa, nec semper lorem quam in massa.

### Removing the title[¶](#removing-the-title "Permanent link")

Similar to [changing the title](#changing-the-title), the icon and title can be omitted entirely by adding an empty string directly after the type qualifier. Note that this will not work for [collapsible blocks](#collapsible-blocks):

Admonition without title

`[](#__codelineno-6-1)!!! note ""   [](#__codelineno-6-3)    Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Nulla et euismod [](#__codelineno-6-4)    nulla. Curabitur feugiat, tortor non consequat finibus, justo purus auctor [](#__codelineno-6-5)    massa, nec semper lorem quam in massa.` 

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Nulla et euismod nulla. Curabitur feugiat, tortor non consequat finibus, justo purus auctor massa, nec semper lorem quam in massa.

### Collapsible blocks[¶](#collapsible-blocks "Permanent link")

When [Details](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/extensions/python-markdown-extensions/#details) is enabled and an admonition block is started with `???` instead of `!!!`, the admonition is rendered as a collapsible block with a small toggle on the right side:

Admonition, collapsible

`[](#__codelineno-7-1)??? note   [](#__codelineno-7-3)    Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Nulla et euismod [](#__codelineno-7-4)    nulla. Curabitur feugiat, tortor non consequat finibus, justo purus auctor [](#__codelineno-7-5)    massa, nec semper lorem quam in massa.` 

Note

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Nulla et euismod nulla. Curabitur feugiat, tortor non consequat finibus, justo purus auctor massa, nec semper lorem quam in massa.

Adding a `+` after the `???` token renders the block expanded:

Admonition, collapsible and initially expanded

`[](#__codelineno-8-1)???+ note   [](#__codelineno-8-3)    Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Nulla et euismod [](#__codelineno-8-4)    nulla. Curabitur feugiat, tortor non consequat finibus, justo purus auctor [](#__codelineno-8-5)    massa, nec semper lorem quam in massa.` 

Note

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Nulla et euismod nulla. Curabitur feugiat, tortor non consequat finibus, justo purus auctor massa, nec semper lorem quam in massa.

### Inline blocks[¶](#inline-blocks "Permanent link")

Admonitions can also be rendered as inline blocks (e.g., for sidebars), placing them to the right using the `inline` \+ `end` modifiers, or to the left using only the `inline` modifier:

Lorem ipsum

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Nulla et euismod nulla. Curabitur feugiat, tortor non consequat finibus, justo purus auctor massa, nec semper lorem quam in massa.

`[](#__codelineno-9-1)!!! info inline end "Lorem ipsum"   [](#__codelineno-9-3)    Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur [](#__codelineno-9-4)    adipiscing elit. Nulla et euismod nulla. [](#__codelineno-9-5)    Curabitur feugiat, tortor non consequat [](#__codelineno-9-6)    finibus, justo purus auctor massa, nec [](#__codelineno-9-7)    semper lorem quam in massa.` 

Use `inline end` to align to the right (left for rtl languages).

Lorem ipsum

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Nulla et euismod nulla. Curabitur feugiat, tortor non consequat finibus, justo purus auctor massa, nec semper lorem quam in massa.

`[](#__codelineno-10-1)!!! info inline "Lorem ipsum"   [](#__codelineno-10-3)    Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur [](#__codelineno-10-4)    adipiscing elit. Nulla et euismod nulla. [](#__codelineno-10-5)    Curabitur feugiat, tortor non consequat [](#__codelineno-10-6)    finibus, justo purus auctor massa, nec [](#__codelineno-10-7)    semper lorem quam in massa.` 

Use `inline` to align to the left (right for rtl languages).

**Important**: admonitions that use the `inline` modifiers _must_ be declared prior to the content block you want to place them beside. If there's insufficient space to render the admonition next to the block, the admonition will stretch to the full width of the viewport, e.g., on mobile viewports.

Following is a list of type qualifiers provided by Material for MkDocs, whereas the default type, and thus fallback for unknown type qualifiers, is `note`[1](#fn:1):

[`note`](#type:note)

items.title: Noisy Anchor Links (`#__codelineno-*`) in Crawled Markdown Consume Excessive Tokens
items.body:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `performance`, `data-quality`

The current implementation crawls web pages (often documentation sites) using `crawl4ai` and stores the resulting Markdown content in the Supabase `crawled_pages` table. However, the Markdown generated, particularly from pages with code examples, frequently contains a large number of self-referential anchor links, primarily targeting specific code line numbers (e.g., `#__codelineno-*`).

While these links might be useful for navigation on the original webpage, they add significant noise to the text stored in the database and processed by downstream language models.

**Example of Noisy Content:**

Here's a snippet from the `content` column for a chunk crawled from the LangGraph documentation, demonstrating the issue:

```markdown
This chunk is the "Supervisor" section of the LangGraph multi-agent system documentation, explaining how to create and use a supervisor-based multi-agent architecture with code examples using the langgraph-supervisor library.
---
## Supervisor[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/agents/multi-agent/#supervisor "Permanent link")
![Supervisor](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/agents/assets/supervisor.png)
Use [`langgraph-supervisor`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph-supervisor-py) library to create a supervisor multi-agent system:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/agents/multi-agent/#__codelineno-0-1)pipinstalllanggraph-supervisor # <<< NOISY LINK

```

_API Reference:[ChatOpenAI](...) | [create_react_agent](...) | [create_supervisor](...)_

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/agents/multi-agent/#__codelineno-1-1)fromlangchain_openaiimport ChatOpenAI # <<< NOISY LINK
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/agents/multi-agent/#__codelineno-1-2)fromlanggraph.prebuiltimport create_react_agent # <<< NOISY LINK
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/agents/multi-agent/#__codelineno-1-3)fromlanggraph_supervisorimport create_supervisor # <<< NOISY LINK
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/agents/multi-agent/#__codelineno-1-4) # <<< NOISY LINK
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/agents/multi-agent/#__codelineno-1-5)defbook_hotel(hotel_name: str): # <<< NOISY LINK
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/agents/multi-agent/#__codelineno-1-6)"""Book a hotel""" # <<< NOISY LINK
# ... and many more similar links ...

```
**Impact:**

This noise has several negative consequences:

1.  **Increased Token Consumption:** These anchor links significantly increase the character count and, consequently, the token count of the stored chunks. This impacts:
    *   The text used for generating embeddings (potentially making them less focused).
    *   The context provided to LLMs during RAG retrieval, consuming valuable context window space.
    *   The cost of embedding API calls and LLM inference calls.
2.  **Reduced Context Quality:** The noisy links dilute the actual meaningful content within the context window provided to the LLM.
3.  **Low Semantic Value:** These specific `#__codelineno-*` links provide little to no semantic value for an LLM trying to understand the code or documentation content.

**Proposed Solution:**

Implement a cleaning step to remove these specific noisy anchor links *before* the content is used for embedding generation (including contextual summary generation) and before it is stored in the `content` column in Supabase.

This can be achieved by adding a cleaning function in `src/utils.py` and applying it within the `add_documents_to_supabase` function.

**Suggested Implementation (`src/utils.py`):**
```
```python
import re

def clean_markdown_noise(markdown_text: str) -> str:
    """Removes specific noisy URL patterns often generated by crawlers."""
    # Pattern targets empty markdown links pointing specifically to #__codelineno anchors
    pattern = r'\[\]\(https?://[^)]*#__codelineno-[^)]+\)\s*'
    cleaned_text = re.sub(pattern, '', markdown_text)
    # Potentially add other cleaning steps here if needed in the future
    return cleaned_text.strip() # Also strip leading/trailing whitespace

# In add_documents_to_supabase function:
# ... inside the batch loop ...
batch_contents_original = contents[i:batch_end]
batch_contents_cleaned = [clean_markdown_noise(c) for c in batch_contents_original]

# Use batch_contents_cleaned for:
# 1. Input to contextual embedding generation (if enabled)
# 2. Input to create_embeddings_batch
# 3. Storing in the 'content' column of the database payload
# ...
```

**Expected Behavior:**

After implementing this change, the `content` stored in the `crawled_pages` table should be free of the `[](...#__codelineno-...)` anchor links. The text used to generate embeddings will also be cleaned, leading to potentially more focused embeddings and significantly reduced token usage when retrieving and using these chunks as context for LLMs.

**Environment:**

*   Project: `mcp-crawl4ai-rag`
*   Relevant Files: `src/utils.py`, `src/crawl4ai_mcp.py`

**Additional Context:**

This enhancement will improve the overall efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and potentially the retrieval quality of the RAG system provided by this MCP server.

items.title: Fix the errors that fail the PDF build in strict mode
items.body:
`mkdocs build --strict` failed at the end with `RuntimeError: 43 error(s) and/or 15 warning(s) occurred while generating PDF.` The with-pdf plugin counts these errors but doesn't print them. They came from two places where the plugin combines pages.

**Root causes**
- **Code line anchors (42 WeasyPrint errors, `No anchor #…:__codelineno-… for internal URI reference`).** When `anchor_linenums` is on, code blocks render `<a id="__codelineno-0-1" name="__codelineno-0-1">`. with-pdf rewrites the `id` and the matching `href`s to page-scoped values, but it leaves `name` alone. For an `<a>`, WeasyPrint uses `name` as the anchor instead of `id`, so none of the line links had a target. This hit the Traefik page and the IoT-HSM Installation page.
- **glightbox image links (1 error + 15 warnings, `Missing 15 link(s)`).** glightbox wraps every image in a link to the image file. with-pdf doesn't change those relative links, so they go nowhere in the PDF, and its strict check reports each one as missing.

**Fix**
A MkDocs hook (`hooks/pdf.py`, registered under `hooks:` in `mkdocs.yml`) runs after with-pdf has captured each page. It changes only the PDF copy of the page: it removes the stale `name` attributes and unwraps the glightbox links. The HTML site doesn't change, so lightbox and line-number links still work there.

I couldn't fix this with CSS in `templates/styles.scss`. WeasyPrint gives the `id`/`name` anchor the same priority as an inline style, and `-weasy-anchor` only accepts a string, not `attr()`. The links are still flagged before with-pdf's `pdf_event_hook` runs, so that hook can't fix them either.

**Verification** (mkdocs 1.6.1, mkdocs-material 9.7.7, mkdocs-with-pdf 0.9.3, WeasyPrint 70.0, Python 3.14)
- The PDF step now logs no errors or warnings, and the `RuntimeError` is gone.
- `mkdocs build --strict` still stops with `Aborted with 1 warnings in strict mode!`. That warning is the existing nav entry `Download PDF: pdf/document.pdf` not being found in the docs, and it already happens on master. This PR doesn't change it.
- The PDF is complete and matches master: 71 pages, the same text, and all 15 screenshots embedded. It no longer has the 30 link annotations that pointed at relative image paths, and the line-number links now resolve.
- On the HTML site, the glightbox wrappers and the code-line anchors are still there.

### Strict-mode nav warning
The `Download PDF` nav entry pointed at `pdf/document.pdf`, which doesn't exist when MkDocs validates the nav (the PDF is generated afterwards), so strict builds aborted with a warning. It now links to `/pdf/document.pdf`. MkDocs logs absolute nav links as info, and the site is served from the root of docs.pkiaas.io. `mkdocs build --strict` now completes with exit code 0. `.gitignore` also ignores the hook's `__pycache__/`.

items.title: feat(docs): site configuration fixes and a strict docs build (#701)
items.body:
Closes #701

## What

Take a page that embeds `docs/examples/predicates.py:filtering`. Today the reader sees

```text
        adults = await User.where(lambda user: user.age >= 18).all()
```

with eight leading spaces, because the example section sits inside `async def main():`. After this PR it starts at column 0, so a pasted block runs. The rest of the PR is configuration of the same kind:

- One click on "Annotated" switches every Assignment/Annotated pair on the site, and tab anchors read `#defining-a-model-annotated` instead of `#__tabbed_1_2`.
- Hovering DDL, RLS, FK, PK, GUC, FFI, IR and similar terms shows a definition, from `docs/includes/abbreviations.md`, appended to every page.
- `#647` in the changelog links to the issue. Permalinks carry a title for screen readers.
- `/guide/migrations/#auto-migration` now lands on `/guide/schema/auto-migrate/` through a generated redirect page. The hand-written stub page is deleted, so it is gone from the sitemap and search. All 16 old anchors are mapped.
- The API reference drops source blocks, puts typed and linked signatures under each heading, and shows summaries, symbol badges and backlinks. `Field` renders once, without its six overloads, and each parameter gets an anchor (`ferro.Field(index)`). `Relation.all()` and `.first()` inherit `Query`'s docstrings.
- Theme: instant navigation with a progress bar, anchor tracking, breadcrumbs, prev/next footer, line selection, "Copy as Markdown", a third "follow system" palette state, GitHub and PyPI footer links, and `new`/`deprecated` status badges. `search.suggest` is removed because nothing reads it.
- Plugins: `redirects`, `llmstxt` (`/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, a `.md` copy of every page) and `social` cards on the rust background `#B7410E` (checked: the card's first pixel is `b7410e`).
- `create`, `upsert`, `get_or_create` and `update_or_create` annotate `**fields: Any`, which clears the griffe warnings.
- The docs build runs with `--strict` in the publish workflow and in a new `docs` job in CI, which `All Checks Passed` now requires.

## Test scenarios

- Happy path: `tests/test_docs_site.py` builds the site with `zensical build --strict` once per session in a temporary directory and passes (13 tests).
- Error path: with `dedent_subsections = false` the indentation test fails and names `/getting-started/quickstart/` (`    await connect("sqlite::memory:", auto_migrate=True)`). With the griffe extension removed, the `Relation` test fails because `Relation.all` has no docstring. I ran both by hand and then restored the config.
- Integration: the generated `guide/migrations/` page maps every old anchor to the section that replaced it. The test resolves each target against the old URL and checks that the anchor exists on the target page.

## Verify

Ran the ticket's Verify block on `d48d7cc`: passed (`No issues found`; 13 passed).
TDD: RED `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_docs_site.py -q --no-cov -p no:cacheprovider` failed as expected on `13629e7` (3 failed, 10 errors: no glossary, a non-strict build, the stub page present). GREEN: the same command passed 13/13 on `d48d7cc`. Full suite: 3309 passed, 339 skipped, 2 xfailed.
Verify block corrected: no

## Interfaces

Interfaces changed: none

`built_site` (session fixture returning the site `Path`) and `rendered_pages(built_site) -> Iterator[tuple[str, str]]` are in `tests/test_docs_site.py`. `url_path` reads like `/guide/queries/`, and `/` for the home page. Zensical refuses a `docs_dir` outside the project root, so the fixture copies `zensical.toml`, `docs/pages` and `docs/includes` into the temp project and symlinks `docs/examples`, `src`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Notes for the reviewer

- **`filters = ["!^_"]`, not `"public"`.** The ticket asks for `filters = "public"` and also for a Model page with no dunders or `__ferro_*__` attributes, and one setting cannot deliver both. Griffe counts every dunder as public, so `"public"` still rendered `__ferro_checks__`, `__getattr__`, `__repr__`, `__post_init__` and the rest. `["!^_"]` hides them. Every API directive names a class or function, never a module, so `__all__` (the one thing `"public"` adds) does not come into play. Site-wide this also hides protocol dunders a reader might care about: `Session.__aenter__`, `Rows.__len__`/`__iter__`/`__getitem__`, and the `AggregateExpr` comparisons. Those belong in the class docstrings, which is #722's work. The reasoning is also in a comment in `zensical.toml`.
- **Outside Files owned:**
  - `docs/pages/api/fields.md`: the `show_overloads: false` / `parameter_headings: true` options the ticket asks for go on the `::: ferro.Field` directive, which lives in that file.
  - `ci.yml`'s two pytest jobs now also sync the `docs` group, so `test_docs_site.py` runs in CI and is not skipped. The file uses `pytest.importorskip("zensical")` for environments without the group.
- The strict build needed no docstring fixes.
- Duplicate `__codelineno-0-N` ids on API pages are still there. `separate_signature` code blocks are all numbered from 0, which the audit flagged as a separate ticket. Strict mode does not flag them.
- `llmstxt` still lists `getting-started/next-steps.md`. The nav ticket (#723) folds that page away and should update the section list.

## Exit steps

- [ ] Issue #701 status updated (closed by the orchestrator after this PR merges into `feat/docs-rewrite`)

items.title: open_quantum: account catalogue, circuit-free estimates and captured docs
items.body:
Open Quantum is the third hardware service the repository reaches: one SDK key reaches IonQ Forte-1 and Forte Enterprise, Rigetti Cepheus-1-108Q, IQM Garnet and Emerald, and AQT IBEX Q1.

- `scripts/oq_platform.py snapshot` makes only reads under the OQ environment's SDK key: providers, backend classes with their full constraint documents and shot schemas, job categories, the 13 MCP tool schemas, and organization-free balances. It also calls the scheduler's circuit-free `POST /v1/pricing/estimate`, the same call the pricing calculator makes, at each backend's shot bounds and at 100, 128, 1000, 1024 and 4096 shots. Nothing is uploaded and no preparation or job is created.
